editorial:
Hoppity Goes to Town is a 1941 animated feature from Fleischer Studios. Paramount Pictures was its 1941 distributor, and it was released under the title Mr. Bug Goes to Town. It follows Hoppity the grasshopper, who returns to Manhattan.

The rights picture is not settled. The film was released in 1941, so it is not public domain by term. Any claim that it is free rests on a missing renewal, which could have been filed in 1968, 1969 or 1970. No complete renewal search has been done. The 1968, 1969 and 1970 catalog volumes and the Copyright Office catalog have not been fully searched. Who filed a renewal, if anyone did, is unknown until those records are searched. Copies on the Internet Archive prove nothing about status. Check the renewal record yourself before any commercial reuse. Separate registrations for the music are a second thing to check.
faq: Is Hoppity Goes to Town safe to reuse commercially?

Not yet. No complete renewal check has been done. The 1968, 1969 and 1970 renewal records and the Copyright Office public catalog still need to be searched. The renewal claimant, if one exists, is unknown until then. Do the searches yourself before relying on it.
Does the Internet Archive upload mean the film is free to use?

No. The Internet Archive hosts both uploads, but hosting does not decide copyright status. Treat them as viewing copies. A different copy or release could carry its own protection, which was not checked.
